properties.foundation_analysis: Bedrock comprises Carboniferous sedimentary strata of the Inverleith Formation (sandstones, siltstones, mudstones) overlain by dense Quaternary glacial till. Building fabric utilizes pale buff-grey Craigleith and Hailes sandstone, characterized by high-silica quartz matrix. Bedding mortar is non-hydraulic hot-mixed lime with local aggregate; subterranean drainage manages high moisture retention in compacted till subsoil.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Charlotte Square Garden perimeter retains mature *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore) and *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime). Canopy phenology for late September: full-volume crowns showing early autumn senescence, localized chlorosis with margins yellowing, minimal leaf-drop, exposing rough grey-brown fissured bark.

properties.architectural_summary:
Neoclassical urban terrace and civic monumentality (Robert Adam design executed by Robert Reid, completed 1814). Rectified vertical planes throughout:
- Center background features West Register House (former St. George's Church): monumental square base with Ionic portico, stepped podium, circular stone drum punctuated by round-arched niches, crowned by a hemispherical copper dome and stone lantern.
- Attached flanking terraces: 3-storey over raised basement with attic storeys. Channelled rustication on ground floors, smooth Craigleith ashlar upper storeys, continuous stringcourses, modillion cornices, and balustraded roof parapets. 
- Fenestration: rectified 6-over-6 and 12-over-12 double-hung timber sash-and-case windows set in regular grid bays with clean ashlar architraves.
